The paper's model is a log-normal race (LNR, `analysis/models/lnr.rds`).
This report sets the DDM-5 (`analysis/models/ddm5.rds`; `ddm5` in
`analysis/server/models.R`) against it, to decide whether the paper should
switch to it: does it fit the data better, does it sample better, and does it
tell the group story more clearly? Both models have the same fixed part
(Group × a strength × difficulty surface per illusion on every parameter), the
full participant surface on the drift, priors from IllusionGameComputational
by the same rules, and the same 55,937 trials. Everything is computed here,
for both fits, by the same code (`analysis/server/marginals.R`), except the
LNR's participant estimates, which are read from
`analysis/results/lnr_participants.csv` (`4_lnr_correlates.qmd`). The DDM-5's
numbers are written to `analysis/results/ddm5_*.csv`. Render from the repo
root (about 20 min; it needs cogmod ≥ 0.3.6):

```bash
quarto render analysis/5_ddm_vs_lnr.qmd
```

The answer is in the last section, "Summary: should the paper switch?".

## The two models side by side

Both are models of the choice and the response time together, with an outlier
component (`poutlier`, with no Group term) for the responses neither process
explains. They put the same questions into different parameters:

| Question | LNR | DDM-5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Time outside the decision (encoding, motor) | `ndt` | `ndt` |
| How well the targets are told apart | discriminability δ = ν₀ − ν₁, the correct accumulator's advantage | the drift towards the correct response, v = −`mu` (`dec(Error)` puts the error on the upper boundary) |
| How much evidence is gathered before responding | none directly: the threshold is fixed at 1, and the overall speed (ν₀ + ν₁) / 2 stands in for (inverse) caution | the boundary separation `boundary` |
| A response favoured before the evidence | none (`sigmabias = 0`) | the start point `bias`, as a share of the boundary from the correct one (> 0.5: closer to the error) |
| Trial-to-trial noise | σ₀ and σ₁, the spread of each accumulator's log-rate | `sigmadrift`, the spread of the drift across trials |
| P(error) | Φ(−δ / √(σ₀² + σ₁²)), closed form | the probability of reaching the error boundary first, averaged over the trial-to-trial drift (quadrature, `igsa_ddm_perror()`) |
| Illusion magnitude | the strength slope of δ over its difficulty slope, at strength 0 and mid difficulty | the same ratio on v |

Every parameter of both models varies with strength and difficulty, as the
LNR's do in the paper.

```{r}
library(brms)
library(ggplot2)

# Runs from analysis/ (quarto) or from the repo root (interactively).
root <- if (dir.exists("server")) "." else "analysis"
source(file.path(root, "server/models.R"))
source(file.path(root, "server/marginals.R"))
stopifnot(utils::packageVersion("cogmod") >= "0.3.6")

out_dir <- file.path(root, "results")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

fits <- list(
  LNR = readRDS(Sys.getenv("IGSA_FIT_LNR", unset = file.path(root, "models/lnr.rds"))),
  "DDM-5" = readRDS(Sys.getenv("IGSA_FIT_DDM", unset = file.path(root, "models/ddm5.rds")))
)
ddm <- fits[["DDM-5"]]

# The same trials, in the same order, or nothing below is comparable.
cols <- c("Participant", "Group", "Illusion_Type", "Illusion_Strength", "Task_Difficulty", "RT", "Error")
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(fits$LNR$data[cols], ddm$data[cols], check.attributes = FALSE)))
trials <- ddm$data
```

```{r}
# Labels and colours. Never is the reference, in neutral grey; each contrast
# against it takes the other group's hue (as in 3_lnr_groups.qmd). The two
# models take two further slots, violet and green, and a line type each.
group_col <- c(Never = "#7a7a75", Past = "#2a78d6", Recent = "#eb6834")

                  "Recent - Past" = "#1baf7a")
model_col <- c(LNR = "#6250d6", "DDM-5" = "#008300")

illusions <- c(Ebbinghaus = "Ebbinghaus", MullerLyer = "Müller-Lyer",
               VerticalHorizontal = "Vertical-Horizontal")
ill_all <- c(illusions, All = "All illusions")

theme_igsa <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#ebebe8", linewidth = 0.3),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = "#6b6b66", hjust = 0)
  )

fmt_ci <- function(m, lo, hi, digits = 2) {
  f <- paste0("%.", digits, "f [%.", digits, "f, %.", digits, "f]")
  sprintf(f, m, lo, hi)
}
```

## Sampling

Both fits ran on the cluster with cmdstanr: 1,500 warmup and 1,000 kept
iterations per chain, 2 chains per shard, 8 threads per chain. The LNR has 8
shards (16 chains); the DDM-5 has 4 (8 chains). From the cluster logs, the
LNR's shards took 7.4 to 32.1 h each and the DDM-5's 4.3 to 5.2 h.

```{r}
diagnostics <- function(m) {
  b <- posterior::summarise_draws(as_draws_array(m, variable = "^b_", regex = TRUE),
                                  "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")
  r <- posterior::summarise_draws(as_draws_array(m, variable = "^r_", regex = TRUE),
                                  "rhat", "ess_bulk")
  np <- nuts_params(m)
  data.frame(
    Chains = nchains(m),
    Draws = ndraws(m),
    Divergent = sum(np$Value[np$Parameter == "divergent__"]),
    "At max tree depth" = sum(np$Value[np$Parameter == "treedepth__"] >= 10),
    "Population: n" = nrow(b),
    "max Rhat" = sprintf("%.3f", max(b$rhat)),
    "Rhat > 1.01" = sum(b$rhat > 1.01),
    "min bulk ESS" = round(min(b$ess_bulk)),
    "min bulk ESS / draw" = sprintf("%.3f", min(b$ess_bulk) / ndraws(m)),
    "min tail ESS" = round(min(b$ess_tail)),
    "Participant: n" = nrow(r),
    "max Rhat " = sprintf("%.3f", max(r$rhat, na.rm = TRUE)),
    "Rhat > 1.01 " = sum(r$rhat > 1.01, na.rm = TRUE),
    "min bulk ESS " = round(min(r$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}
diag_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fits, diagnostics))
knitr::kable(t(diag_tab), col.names = names(fits))
```

The population rows are the `b_` coefficients; the participant rows the `r_`
deviations. The LNR has twice the chains, so its effective sample sizes should
be read per draw.

## Fit to the data

### Predictive accuracy

Leave-one-trial-out cross-validation (PSIS-LOO) on about 1,000 posterior
draws per model, spread evenly over the chains. The log-likelihood is the
joint density of the response time and the choice, outlier component
included, so the two models are on the same scale. Higher is better.

```{r}
# Evenly spaced draws within each chain, so that loo can estimate the
# relative efficiency from the chains.
per_chain_ids <- function(m, total = 1000) {
  k <- ceiling(total / nchains(m))
  n_iter <- ndraws(m) / nchains(m)
  list(ids = unlist(lapply(seq_len(nchains(m)) - 1, function(c) c * n_iter + round(seq(1, n_iter, length.out = k)))),
       chain = rep(seq_len(nchains(m)), each = k))
}

# brms::log_lik() calls the family once per trial; cogmod's densities are
# vectorised, so this computes the same numbers (checked to equality on the
# first 300 trials) in blocks of draws.
loglik <- function(m, ids, chunk = 250) {
  pars <- igsa_pars(m)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(split(ids, ceiling(seq_along(ids) / chunk)), function(i) {
    p <- lapply(setNames(pars, pars), function(q) posterior_linpred(m, dpar = q, transform = TRUE, draw_ids = i))
    x <- rep(m$data$RT, each = length(i))
    r <- rep(m$data$Error, each = length(i))
    ll <- if (m$family$name == "cogmod_ddm") {
      cogmod::dcogmod_ddm(x, drift = p$mu, boundary = p$boundary, bias = p$bias, ndt = p$ndt, response = r,
                          sigmadrift = p$sigmadrift, poutlier = p$poutlier, log = TRUE)
    } else {
      cogmod::dcogmod_lnr(x, nuzero = p$mu, nuone = p$nuone, sigmazero = p$sigmazero, sigmaone = p$sigmaone,
                          ndt = p$ndt, response = r, poutlier = p$poutlier, log = TRUE)
    }
    matrix(ll, nrow = length(i))
  }))
}

check_ids <- c(5, 500)
for (m in fits) {
  stopifnot(max(abs(loglik(m, check_ids)[, 1:300] -
                    log_lik(m, draw_ids = check_ids, newdata = m$data[1:300, ]))) < 1e-8)
}

loos <- lapply(fits, function(m) {
  s <- per_chain_ids(m)
  ll <- loglik(m, s$ids)
  loo::loo(ll, r_eff = loo::relative_eff(exp(ll), chain_id = s$chain))
})
cmp <- loo::loo_compare(loos)

loo_tab <- data.frame(
  Model = names(loos),
  Draws = sapply(loos, function(l) attr(l, "dims")[1]),
  elpd_loo = sapply(loos, function(l) l$estimates["elpd_loo", "Estimate"]),
  SE = sapply(loos, function(l) l$estimates["elpd_loo", "SE"]),
  p_loo = sapply(loos, function(l) l$estimates["p_loo", "Estimate"]),
  "Pareto k > 0.7" = sapply(loos, function(l) sum(loo::pareto_k_values(l) > 0.7)),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
)
# loo >= 2.9 names the models in a `model` column; older versions in the row names.
cmp <- as.data.frame(cmp)
cmp$Model <- if ("model" %in% names(cmp)) cmp$model else rownames(cmp)
loo_tab$elpd_diff <- cmp$elpd_diff[match(loo_tab$Model, cmp$Model)]
loo_tab$se_diff <- cmp$se_diff[match(loo_tab$Model, cmp$Model)]
write.csv(loo_tab, file.path(out_dir, "ddm5_vs_lnr_loo.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(loo_tab, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE)

best <- cmp$Model[1]
elpd_gap <- -cmp$elpd_diff[2]
elpd_gap_se <- cmp$se_diff[2]
high_k <- setNames(loo_tab$"Pareto k > 0.7", loo_tab$Model)
```

The `r best` is ahead by `r sprintf("%.0f", elpd_gap)` log units
(SE `r sprintf("%.0f", elpd_gap_se)`), `r sprintf("%.3f", elpd_gap / nrow(trials))`
per trial: a predictive density `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (exp(elpd_gap / nrow(trials)) - 1))`
higher on the average trial. The estimate is approximate:
`r high_k[["LNR"]]` (LNR) and `r high_k[["DDM-5"]]` (DDM-5) trials have a
Pareto k above 0.7, where PSIS is unreliable. Both models have thousands of
effective parameters (p_loo), mostly participant effects, so leaving out one
trial can move its participant's posterior noticeably. An exact comparison
would need K-fold cross-validation, which means refitting.

```{r}
# Where the gap comes from: the pointwise difference, summed per group,
# illusion and strength band, and split by response.
pw <- loos[["DDM-5"]]$pointwise[, "elpd_loo"] - loos$LNR$pointwise[, "elpd_loo"]
band <- function(s) ifelse(s <= -0.6, "Facilitating", ifelse(s >= 0.6, "Conflicting", ifelse(abs(s) <= 0.3, "None", "In between")))
by_cell <- aggregate(cbind(Difference = pw, Trials = 1) ~ Response + Band,
                     data.frame(pw = pw, Response = ifelse(trials$Error == 1, "Error", "Correct"),
                                Band = band(trials$Illusion_Strength)), sum)
by_cell$"Per trial" <- by_cell$Difference / by_cell$Trials
knitr::kable(by_cell[order(by_cell$Response, by_cell$Band), ], digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "elpd_loo, DDM-5 minus LNR (positive: the DDM-5 predicts these trials better)")
```

### Posterior predictive checks

One hundred evenly spaced posterior draws per model simulate a choice and a
response time for every trial, with the participant effects in, as in
`3_lnr_groups.qmd`. The simulated trials are summarised the way the observed
ones are: the error rate and the median response time per pair of
neighbouring strengths (the design is a checkerboard across blocks; see
`3_lnr_groups.qmd`), and the quantiles of correct and of error response times
in three bands of strength (facilitating, strength ≤ −0.6; none, |strength| ≤
0.3; conflicting, strength ≥ 0.6).

```{r}
# posterior_predict() calls the family once per trial; cogmod's methods also
# take a vector of trials and return their draws stacked, trial by trial
# (cogmod's ?rcogmod_ddm, "Predicting many observations at once").
simulate <- function(m, ids) {
  prep <- brms::prepare_predictions(m, draw_ids = ids)
  for (dp in names(prep$dpars)) prep$dpars[[dp]] <- brms::get_dpar(prep, dp)
  fun <- if (m$family$name == "cogmod_ddm") cogmod::posterior_predict_cogmod_ddm else cogmod::posterior_predict_cogmod_lnr
  pp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(seq_len(prep$nobs), ceiling(seq_len(prep$nobs) / 50)), fun, prep = prep))
  n <- length(ids)
  stopifnot(nrow(pp) == n * prep$nobs, all(pp[, 2] %in% c(0, 1)))
  list(rt = matrix(pp[, 1], nrow = n), error = matrix(pp[, 2], nrow = n))
}
set.seed(1)
sims <- lapply(fits, function(m) simulate(m, round(seq(1, ndraws(m), length.out = 100))))

strength_pair <- function(s) sign(s) * (2 * floor((round(10 * abs(s)) - 1) / 2) + 1.5) / 10
key <- paste(trials$Group, trials$Illusion_Type, strength_pair(trials$Illusion_Strength), sep = "|")
curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sims), function(mn) {
  s <- sims[[mn]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(key), function(k) {
    parts <- strsplit(k, "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    i <- which(key == k)
    e <- rowMeans(s$error[, i, drop = FALSE])
    r <- apply(s$rt[, i, drop = FALSE], 1, median)
    head <- data.frame(Model = mn, Group = parts[1], Illusion_Type = parts[2],
                       Illusion_Strength = as.numeric(parts[3]), N = length(i))
    rbind(
      cbind(head, Measure = "Error rate", Observed = mean(trials$Error[i]), Pred_mean = mean(e),
            Pred_low = quantile(e, 0.025), Pred_high = quantile(e, 0.975)),
      cbind(head, Measure = "Median RT (s)", Observed = median(trials$RT[i]), Pred_mean = mean(r),
            Pred_low = quantile(r, 0.025), Pred_high = quantile(r, 0.975)))
  }))
}))
rownames(curves) <- NULL
write.csv(curves[curves$Model == "DDM-5", -1], file.path(out_dir, "ddm5_ppc_curves.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

How far the predictions sit from the observed points (error rates in
percentage points, median RTs in ms), and how many observed points fall
inside the 95% predictive band, over the 180 points per model (3 groups × 3
illusions × 10 pairs of strengths × 2 measures):

```{r}
dev_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(curves, list(curves$Model, curves$Measure)), function(x) {
  k <- if (x$Measure[1] == "Error rate") 100 else 1000
  data.frame(Model = x$Model[1], Measure = x$Measure[1],
             "Mean signed (pred - obs)" = k * mean(x$Pred_mean - x$Observed),
             "Mean absolute" = k * mean(abs(x$Pred_mean - x$Observed)),
             "Largest absolute" = k * max(abs(x$Pred_mean - x$Observed)),
             "Inside the 95% band" = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(x$Observed >= x$Pred_low & x$Observed <= x$Pred_high)),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
dev_tab$Measure <- ifelse(dev_tab$Measure == "Error rate", "Error rate (points)", "Median RT (ms)")
dev_tab <- dev_tab[order(dev_tab$Measure, dev_tab$Model), ]
knitr::kable(dev_tab, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
plot_curves <- function(measure, title) {
  x <- curves[curves$Measure == measure, ]
  x$Illusion_Type <- factor(illusions[x$Illusion_Type], levels = illusions)
  x$Group <- factor(x$Group, levels = names(group_col))
  x$Model <- factor(x$Model, levels = names(fits))
  ggplot(x, aes(Illusion_Strength)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#9a9a95", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Pred_low, ymax = Pred_high, fill = Group), alpha = 0.25) +
    geom_line(aes(y = Pred_mean, colour = Group), linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(y = Observed, colour = Group), size = 1.2) +
    facet_grid(Model ~ Illusion_Type) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = group_col) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = group_col) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-1, 0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "Illusion strength", y = measure, colour = NULL, fill = NULL, title = title,
         caption = paste0("Points: observed, per pair of neighbouring strengths, pooled over difficulty and participants.\n",
                          "Lines and bands: posterior predictive mean and 95% interval (100 draws).")) +
    theme_igsa
}
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5

plot_curves("Error rate", "Error rate across strength, per model")
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5

plot_curves("Median RT (s)", "Median response time across strength, per model")
```

The shape of the response time distributions, which is where the LNR misfits
(`3_lnr_groups.qmd`: the observed distributions are more peaked than its
predictions). For each group, illusion and band, the 10th, 30th, 50th, 70th
and 90th percentiles of the correct and of the error response times, observed
against predicted (the mean over the 100 draws of each draw's percentile).
Cells with fewer than 30 observed responses of the kind are left out, which
removes the errors on facilitating trials.

```{r}
probs <- c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9)
trials$Band <- band(trials$Illusion_Strength)
qcell <- paste(trials$Group, trials$Illusion_Type, trials$Band, sep = "|")
qcells <- unique(qcell[trials$Band != "In between"])
quantiles <- do.call(rbind, lapply(qcells, function(k) {
  parts <- strsplit(k, "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  i <- which(qcell == k)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c(Correct = 0, Error = 1), function(r) {
    obs <- trials$RT[i][trials$Error[i] == r]
    if (length(obs) < 30) return(NULL)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sims), function(mn) {
      s <- sims[[mn]]
      pq <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(s$rt)), function(j) {
        x <- s$rt[j, i][s$error[j, i] == r]
        if (length(x) < 5) rep(NA_real_, length(probs)) else stats::quantile(x, probs, names = FALSE)
      }, numeric(length(probs))))
      data.frame(Model = mn, Group = parts[1], Illusion_Type = parts[2], Band = parts[3],
                 Response = if (r == 1) "Error" else "Correct", N = length(obs), Quantile = probs,
                 Observed = stats::quantile(obs, probs, names = FALSE),
                 Pred_mean = colMeans(pq, na.rm = TRUE),
                 Pred_low = apply(pq, 2, stats::quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
                 Pred_high = apply(pq, 2, stats::quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))
    }))
  }))
}))
write.csv(quantiles, file.path(out_dir, "ddm5_vs_lnr_ppc_quantiles.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

q_tab <- aggregate(list(Deviation = 1000 * (quantiles$Pred_mean - quantiles$Observed),
                        Absolute = 1000 * abs(quantiles$Pred_mean - quantiles$Observed),
                        Inside = quantiles$Observed >= quantiles$Pred_low & quantiles$Observed <= quantiles$Pred_high),
                   list(Model = quantiles$Model, Response = quantiles$Response, Quantile = quantiles$Quantile), mean)
q_wide <- stats::reshape(q_tab, idvar = c("Response", "Quantile"), timevar = "Model", direction = "wide")
q_wide <- q_wide[order(q_wide$Response, q_wide$Quantile), ]
q_wide$Quantile <- paste0(100 * q_wide$Quantile, "th")
for (mn in names(fits)) q_wide[[paste0("Inside.", mn)]] <- sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * q_wide[[paste0("Inside.", mn)]])
knitr::kable(q_wide[c("Response", "Quantile", paste0(c("Deviation.", "Absolute.", "Inside."), "LNR"),
                      paste0(c("Deviation.", "Absolute.", "Inside."), "DDM-5"))],
             digits = 0, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Response", "Percentile", "LNR: mean (pred - obs), ms", "LNR: mean absolute", "LNR: inside 95%",
                           "DDM-5: mean (pred - obs), ms", "DDM-5: mean absolute", "DDM-5: inside 95%"))
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9

qx <- quantiles

  theme_igsa
```

The distributions themselves with no illusion (|strength| ≤ 0.3), the band
where the LNR's misfit was clearest: correct responses above the axis, errors
below, each as a share of all responses (50 ms bins).

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7.5

breaks <- seq(0, 2.5, by = 0.05)
tgrid <- breaks[-1] - diff(breaks) / 2
defective <- function(rt, err, r) tabulate(findInterval(rt[err == r], breaks), nbins = length(tgrid)) / length(rt) / diff(breaks)
none <- trials$Band == "None"
dcell <- paste(trials$Group, trials$Illusion_Type, sep = "|")
dens <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(dcell[none]), function(k) {
  parts <- strsplit(k, "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  i <- which(dcell == k & none)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c(Correct = 0, Error = 1), function(r) {
    s <- if (r == 1) -1 else 1
    rbind(
      data.frame(Source = "Observed", Group = parts[1], Illusion_Type = parts[2], Response = r, RT = tgrid,
                 Density = s * defective(trials$RT[i], trials$Error[i], r)),
      do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sims), function(mn) {
        M <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(sims[[mn]]$rt)), function(j) defective(sims[[mn]]$rt[j, i], sims[[mn]]$error[j, i], r),
                      numeric(length(tgrid))))
        data.frame(Source = mn, Group = parts[1], Illusion_Type = parts[2], Response = r, RT = tgrid,
                   Density = s * colMeans(M))
      })))
  }))
}))
dens$Illusion_Type <- factor(illusions[dens$Illusion_Type], levels = illusions)
dens$Group <- factor(dens$Group, levels = names(group_col))
obs <- dens[dens$Source == "Observed", ]
pred <- dens[dens$Source != "Observed", ]
pred$Model <- factor(pred$Source, levels = names(fits))

ggplot(pred, aes(RT, Density)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#9a9a95", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_col(data = obs, aes(group = Response), fill = "#c9c8c2", width = 0.045) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = Model, linetype = Model, group = interaction(Model, Response)), linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(Group ~ Illusion_Type) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = model_col) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = model_lty) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(y) abs(y)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 2)) +
  labs(x = "Response time (s)", y = "Density: correct above, errors below", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
       title = "Response time distributions with no illusion",
       caption = "Bars: observed (50 ms bins). Lines: posterior predictive mean of each model (100 draws).") +
  theme_igsa
```

```{r}
rm(sims)
invisible(gc())
```

## Group differences

### The DDM-5's parameters across strength

Each group's DDM-5 parameters at the population level, across illusion
strength at mid difficulty (the LNR's are in `3_lnr_groups.qmd`).

```{r}
quantities_ddm <- c(
  delta = "v: drift towards the correct response",
  boundary = "a: boundary separation",
  bias = "w: start point (share of a, from the correct boundary)",
  ndt = "Non-decision time (s)",
  sigmadrift = "sv: trial-to-trial drift SD",
  perror = "P(error)"
)
grid <- igsa_grid(ddm, strength = round(seq(-1, 1, by = 0.1), 2), difficulty = 0)
d <- igsa_draws(ddm, grid)
surface <- igsa_summary(d, grid, what = names(quantities_ddm))
write.csv(igsa_summary(d, grid), file.path(out_dir, "ddm5_groups_means.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 11

sx <- surface
sx$Quantity <- factor(quantities_ddm[sx$Quantity], levels = quantities_ddm)
sx$Illusion_Type <- factor(illusions[as.character(sx$Illusion_Type)], levels = illusions)
ggplot(sx, aes(Illusion_Strength, Median)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = CI_low, ymax = CI_high, fill = Group), alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = Group), linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(Quantity ~ Illusion_Type, scales = "free_y", switch = "y",
             labeller = labeller(Quantity = label_wrap_gen(22))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_col) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = group_col) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-1, 0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Illusion strength", y = NULL, colour = NULL, fill = NULL, title = "DDM-5 parameters per group",
       caption = paste0("Population level, mid task difficulty. Lines: posterior medians; bands: 95% intervals.\n",
                        "Strength: + pushes towards the error (conflicting), - towards the right answer (facilitating).")) +
  theme_igsa + theme(strip.placement = "outside")
```

```{r}
# How much the parameters that should be set before the stimulus (boundary,
# start point) move with the stimulus: strength -1 against +1, per group,
# averaged over the illusions.
pre <- function(q, s) {
  x <- surface[surface$Quantity == q & surface$Illusion_Strength == s, ]
  tapply(x$Median, x$Group, mean)
}
a_fac <- pre("boundary", -1); a_con <- pre("boundary", 1)
w_fac <- pre("bias", -1); w_con <- pre("bias", 1)
```

The boundary and the start point move with illusion strength. Averaged over
the illusions, Never's boundary is `r sprintf("%.2f", a_fac["Never"])` on
the most facilitating trials and `r sprintf("%.2f", a_con["Never"])` on the
most conflicting ones, and its start point `r sprintf("%.2f", w_fac["Never"])`
and `r sprintf("%.2f", w_con["Never"])`. The illusions are mixed at random
within blocks, so neither can be set in advance for the trial's strength: in
the DDM's own terms these are effects of the stimulus on parameters that
should not depend on it.

### Matched quantities, averaged over the design

The group differences averaged over every strength × difficulty point the
task showed (as in `3_lnr_groups.qmd`), for the quantities the two models
share and for the rest of their parameters. Each cell is the median, the 95%
interval and, in parentheses, the probability of direction (pd).

```{r}
design <- igsa_design_grid(ddm)
averaged <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(mn) {
  dd <- igsa_draws(fits[[mn]], design)
  dd$poutlier <- NULL
  by_ill <- igsa_summary(igsa_contrasts(igsa_average(dd, design)))
  all <- igsa_summary(igsa_contrasts(igsa_average(dd, design, by = "Group")))
  all$Illusion_Type <- "All"
  means_ill <- igsa_summary(igsa_average(dd, design))
  means_all <- igsa_summary(igsa_average(dd, design, by = "Group"))
  means_all$Illusion_Type <- "All"
  if (mn == "DDM-5") {
    cols <- c("Group", "Illusion_Type", "Quantity", "Median", "CI_low", "CI_high", "pd")
    write.csv(rbind(means_ill[cols], means_all[cols]), file.path(out_dir, "ddm5_groups_averaged_means.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  }
  cols <- c("Quantity", "Contrast", "Illusion_Type", "Median", "CI_low", "CI_high", "pd")
  out <- rbind(by_ill[cols], all[cols])
  out$Illusion_Type <- as.character(out$Illusion_Type)
  cbind(Model = mn, out)
}))
write.csv(averaged[averaged$Model == "DDM-5", -1], file.path(out_dir, "ddm5_groups_averaged.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Common labels, and the units the two models share: ms and percentage points.
matched <- rbind(
  data.frame(Model = "LNR", Quantity = c("ndt", "perror", "delta", "speed", "mu", "nuone", "sigmazero", "sigmaone"),
             Label = c("Non-decision time (ms)", "P(error) (points)", "Discriminability", "Caution",
                       "Other", "Other", "Other", "Other"),
             Parameter = c("ndt", "race", "nu0 - nu1", "speed (nu0 + nu1) / 2: lower = more cautious",
                           "nu0: correct drift", "nu1: error drift", "sigma0: correct noise", "sigma1: error noise"),
             Scale = c(1000, 100, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)),
  data.frame(Model = "DDM-5", Quantity = c("ndt", "perror", "delta", "boundary", "bias", "sigmadrift"),
             Label = c("Non-decision time (ms)", "P(error) (points)", "Discriminability", "Caution", "Other", "Other"),
             Parameter = c("ndt", "diffusion", "v = -drift", "boundary a: higher = more cautious",
                           "w: start point", "sv: trial-to-trial drift SD"),
             Scale = c(1000, 100, 1, 1, 1, 1))
)
avg <- merge(averaged, matched, by = c("Model", "Quantity"))
for (v in c("Median", "CI_low", "CI_high")) avg[[v]] <- avg[[v]] * avg$Scale
avg$Value <- sprintf("%s (%.2f)", fmt_ci(avg$Median, avg$CI_low, avg$CI_high), avg$pd)

tab <- avg[avg$Illusion_Type == "All", c("Label", "Model", "Parameter", "Contrast", "Value")]
tab <- stats::reshape(tab, idvar = c("Label", "Model", "Parameter"), timevar = "Contrast", direction = "wide")
names(tab) <- sub("^Value\\.", "", names(tab))
tab <- tab[order(match(tab$Label, unique(matched$Label)), match(tab$Model, names(fits))), ]
knitr::kable(tab[c("Label", "Model", "Parameter", "Past - Never", "Recent - Never", "Recent - Past")],
             row.names = FALSE, col.names = c("Quantity", "Model", "Parameter", "Past - Never", "Recent - Never", "Recent - Past"))
```

The two quantities on a shared scale, per illusion:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6

plot_models <- function(x, title, caption, xlab = "Difference between groups (median, 95% interval)") {
  x$Illusion_Type <- factor(ill_all[as.character(x$Illusion_Type)], levels = c(rev(illusions), "All illusions"))
  x$Model <- factor(x$Model, levels = names(fits))
  x$Dodge <- factor(x$Model, levels = rev(names(fits)))
  ggplot(x, aes(Median, Illusion_Type, colour = Model, group = Dodge)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#9a9a95", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = CI_low, xmax = CI_high, linetype = Model), linewidth = 0.7,
                   position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = Model), size = 2.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.55)) +
    facet_grid(Contrast ~ Panel, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_col) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = model_lty) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(LNR = 17, "DDM-5" = 16)) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = NULL, colour = NULL, linetype = NULL, shape = NULL, title = title, caption = caption) +
    theme_igsa + theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 8))
}
shared <- avg[avg$Label %in% c("Non-decision time (ms)", "P(error) (points)"), ]
shared$Panel <- shared$Label
plot_models(shared, "Group differences averaged over the design",
            "Population level, averaged over every strength x difficulty point shown.")
```

## Illusion sensitivity

### The illusion magnitude

The paper's primary index: at strength 0 and mid difficulty, the effect of
one unit of strength on discriminability over the effect of one unit of
difficulty on it, which is how many units of difficulty one unit of strength
is worth (`igsa_index()`). It is defined the same way on each model's
discriminability (δ for the LNR, v for the DDM-5). Per group and illusion:

```{r}
g4 <- igsa_grid(ddm, strength = c(0, 1), difficulty = c(0, 1))
d4 <- lapply(fits, function(m) igsa_draws(m, g4))
ix <- lapply(d4, function(x) igsa_index(x, g4))

index_means <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ix), function(mn) cbind(Model = mn, igsa_summary(ix[[mn]]))))
index_contrasts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ix), function(mn) cbind(Model = mn, igsa_summary(igsa_contrasts(ix[[mn]])))))

# The same contrasts as a change relative to the reference group, per draw:
# 100 x (a / b - 1). The components are in each model's own units, so this is
# what puts them on one scale.
relative <- function(x, grid = attr(x, "grid"),
                     pairs = list(c("Past", "Never"), c("Recent", "Never"), c("Recent", "Past"))) {
  out <- list()
  rows <- list()
  for (p in pairs) {
    ia <- which(grid$Group == p[1])
    ib <- which(grid$Group == p[2])
    ib <- ib[match(grid$Illusion_Type[ia], grid$Illusion_Type[ib])]
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(Contrast = paste(p, collapse = " - "), Illusion_Type = grid$Illusion_Type[ia])
    for (q in names(x)) out[[q]] <- cbind(out[[q]], 100 * (x[[q]][, ia, drop = FALSE] / x[[q]][, ib, drop = FALSE] - 1))
  }
  attr(out, "grid") <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  out
}
index_relative <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ix), function(mn) cbind(Model = mn, igsa_summary(relative(ix[[mn]])))))

ddm_slopes <- rbind(
  cbind(Kind = "Group value", igsa_summary(ix[["DDM-5"]])[c("Group", "Illusion_Type", "Quantity", "Median", "CI_low", "CI_high", "pd")], Contrast = NA),
  cbind(Kind = "Difference", Group = NA, igsa_summary(igsa_contrasts(ix[["DDM-5"]]))[c("Illusion_Type", "Quantity", "Median", "CI_low", "CI_high", "pd", "Contrast")]),
  cbind(Kind = "Relative difference (%)", Group = NA, igsa_summary(relative(ix[["DDM-5"]]))[c("Illusion_Type", "Quantity", "Median", "CI_low", "CI_high", "pd", "Contrast")])
)
write.csv(ddm_slopes, file.path(out_dir, "ddm5_groups_slopes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

im <- index_means[index_means$Quantity == "index", ]
im$Value <- fmt_ci(im$Median, im$CI_low, im$CI_high)
im$Illusion <- illusions[as.character(im$Illusion_Type)]
im_wide <- stats::reshape(im[c("Illusion", "Model", "Group", "Value")], idvar = c("Illusion", "Model"),
                          timevar = "Group", direction = "wide")
names(im_wide) <- sub("^Value\\.", "", names(im_wide))
knitr::kable(im_wide[order(im_wide$Illusion, match(im_wide$Model, names(fits))), ], row.names = FALSE)
```

Its group differences, in index units and relative to the second group:

```{r}
ic <- merge(index_contrasts[index_contrasts$Quantity == "index", ],
            index_relative[index_relative$Quantity == "index", ],
            by = c("Model", "Contrast", "Illusion_Type", "Quantity"), suffixes = c("", "_rel"))
ic$Difference <- sprintf("%s (%.3f)", fmt_ci(ic$Median, ic$CI_low, ic$CI_high), ic$pd)
ic$Relative <- sprintf("%.0f%% [%.0f, %.0f]", ic$Median_rel, ic$CI_low_rel, ic$CI_high_rel)
ic$Illusion <- illusions[as.character(ic$Illusion_Type)]
ic <- ic[order(ic$Contrast, ic$Illusion, match(ic$Model, names(fits))), ]
knitr::kable(ic[c("Contrast", "Illusion", "Model", "Difference", "Relative")], row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Contrast", "Illusion", "Model", "Difference (pd)", "Relative to the second group"))
```

Where the difference comes from. The index is a ratio, so it can shrink
because the illusion moves discriminability less or because difficulty moves
it more. Both components and the index, as the change relative to Never:

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.5

comp_lab <- c(delta_strength = "Illusion effect on discriminability",
              delta_difficulty = "Precision (difficulty effect)",
              index = "Illusion magnitude (their ratio)")
rx <- index_relative[index_relative$Contrast != "Recent - Past", ]
rx$Panel <- factor(comp_lab[rx$Quantity], levels = comp_lab)
rx$Contrast <- sub(" - Never", " vs Never", rx$Contrast)
plot_models(rx, "The illusion magnitude and its two components, relative to Never",
            paste0("Population level, at strength 0 and mid difficulty. 100 x (group / Never - 1), per draw.\n",
                   "Both components are negative, so a positive value is a larger effect."),
            xlab = "Difference relative to Never (%; median, 95% interval)")
```

### The illusion effect on P(error)

The change in P(error) from strength 0 to 1 at mid difficulty, in percentage
points, per group and as group differences. This is the population level, as
in `3_lnr_groups.qmd` and the paper: a participant whose every random effect
is zero. It is a prediction for a typical participant, not a summary of the
data, and the two models need not agree on it. Averaged over the
participants, both follow the observed error rates (the posterior predictive
checks above). But a typical participant's P(error) depends on how each model
turns its parameters into choices. The participant-averaged version is under
"Participant level" below.

```{r}
pe <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(d4), function(mn) {
  s <- igsa_slopes(d4[[mn]], g4, from = 0, to = 1)
  keep <- attr(s, "grid")$Task_Difficulty == 0
  s0 <- lapply(s["perror"], function(x) 100 * x[, keep, drop = FALSE])
  attr(s0, "grid") <- attr(s, "grid")[keep, c("Group", "Illusion_Type")]
  rbind(cbind(Model = mn, Kind = "Group", igsa_summary(s0), Contrast = NA),
        cbind(Model = mn, Kind = "Contrast", Group = NA, igsa_summary(igsa_contrasts(s0))))
}))
pg <- pe[pe$Kind == "Group", ]
pg$Value <- sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", pg$Median, pg$CI_low, pg$CI_high)
pg$Illusion <- illusions[as.character(pg$Illusion_Type)]
pg_wide <- stats::reshape(pg[c("Illusion", "Model", "Group", "Value")], idvar = c("Illusion", "Model"),
                          timevar = "Group", direction = "wide")
names(pg_wide) <- sub("^Value\\.", "", names(pg_wide))
knitr::kable(pg_wide[order(pg_wide$Illusion, match(pg_wide$Model, names(fits))), ], row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Increase in P(error) from strength 0 to 1, percentage points")
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

pc <- pe[pe$Kind == "Contrast", ]
pc$Panel <- "Illusion effect on P(error), points"
pc$Contrast <- factor(pc$Contrast, levels = names(contrast_col))
plot_models(pc, "Group differences in the illusion effect on P(error)",
            "Population level, mid difficulty: P(error) at strength 1 minus at strength 0.")
```

## Participant level

Per participant and illusion, from 1,000 evenly spaced draws of the DDM-5
with the participant effects in, the same indices as `4_lnr_correlates.qmd`
computes for the LNR, at strength 0 and mid difficulty. The LNR's are its
medians in `analysis/results/lnr_participants.csv`.

```{r}
draw_ids <- round(seq(1, ndraws(ddm), length.out = 1000))
pgrid <- igsa_participant_grid(ddm, strength = c(0, 1), difficulty = c(0, 1))
pd <- igsa_draws(ddm, pgrid, re_formula = NULL, draw_ids = draw_ids)
pd$poutlier <- NULL

cells <- unique(pgrid[c("Participant", "Group", "Illusion_Type")])
cells <- cells[order(cells$Participant, cells$Illusion_Type), ]
rownames(cells) <- NULL
cell_key <- paste(cells$Participant, cells$Illusion_Type)
align <- function(x, grid) x[, match(cell_key, paste(grid$Participant, grid$Illusion_Type)), drop = FALSE]

at00 <- pgrid$Illusion_Strength == 0 & pgrid$Task_Difficulty == 0
base <- lapply(pd, function(x) align(x[, at00, drop = FALSE], pgrid[at00, ]))
pix <- igsa_index(pd, pgrid)
pix <- lapply(pix, align, grid = attr(pix, "grid"))
eff <- igsa_slopes(pd, pgrid, from = 0, to = 1)
eff_grid <- attr(eff, "grid")
eff <- lapply(eff, function(x) align(x[, eff_grid$Task_Difficulty == 0, drop = FALSE],
                                     eff_grid[eff_grid$Task_Difficulty == 0, ]))
nonneg <- colMeans(pix$delta_difficulty >= 0)

pq <- list(
  "Discriminability, no illusion" = base$delta,
  "Boundary, no illusion" = base$boundary,
  "Start point, no illusion" = base$bias,
  "Drift SD, no illusion" = base$sigmadrift,
  "Non-decision time (s), no illusion" = base$ndt,
  "P(error), no illusion" = base$perror,
  "Illusion effect on discriminability" = pix$delta_strength,
  "Illusion effect on P(error)" = eff$perror,
  "Precision (difficulty slope)" = pix$delta_difficulty,
  "Illusion magnitude (strength / difficulty)" = pix$index
)
per_participant <- function(x) {
  idx <- split(seq_len(nrow(cells)), factor(cells$Participant, levels = unique(cells$Participant)))
  sapply(idx, function(i) rowMeans(x[, i, drop = FALSE]))
}
ids <- unique(as.character(cells$Participant))
summarise_cells <- function(x, grid) {
  data.frame(grid, Median = apply(x, 2, stats::median),
             CI_low = apply(x, 2, stats::quantile, probs = 0.025),
             CI_high = apply(x, 2, stats::quantile, probs = 0.975), row.names = NULL)
}
ppt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pq), function(qn) {
  rbind(
    cbind(Quantity = qn, summarise_cells(pq[[qn]], cells)),
    cbind(Quantity = qn, summarise_cells(per_participant(pq[[qn]]), data.frame(
      Participant = ids, Group = cells$Group[match(ids, cells$Participant)], Illusion_Type = "All")))
  )
}))
ppt$Participant <- as.character(ppt$Participant)
ppt$Illusion_Type <- as.character(ppt$Illusion_Type)
write.csv(ppt, file.path(out_dir, "ddm5_participants.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

lnr_ppt <- read.csv(file.path(out_dir, "lnr_participants.csv"))
```

`r sum(nonneg > 0.05)` of `r length(nonneg)` participant × illusion cells
have more than 5% of their DDM-5 draws with a non-negative precision term,
where the index is unstable (maximum share `r sprintf("%.2f", max(nonneg))`);
the index is summarised by its median.

### Do the models rank participants the same way?

The Spearman correlation across participants between the two models'
posterior medians, per illusion. Caution is the LNR's speed against the
DDM-5's boundary, so agreement shows as a negative correlation there.

```{r}
pairs_q <- c(
  "Non-decision time (s), no illusion" = "Non-decision time (s), no illusion",
  "Discriminability, no illusion" = "Discriminability, no illusion",
  "Speed, no illusion" = "Boundary, no illusion",
  "P(error), no illusion" = "P(error), no illusion",
  "Illusion effect on P(error)" = "Illusion effect on P(error)",
  "Precision (difficulty slope)" = "Precision (difficulty slope)",
  "Illusion magnitude (strength / difficulty)" = "Illusion magnitude (strength / difficulty)"
)
agree <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pairs_q), function(lq) {
  a <- lnr_ppt[lnr_ppt$Quantity == lq, c("Participant", "Illusion_Type", "Median")]
  b <- ppt[ppt$Quantity == pairs_q[[lq]], c("Participant", "Illusion_Type", "Median")]
  x <- merge(a, b, by = c("Participant", "Illusion_Type"), suffixes = c("_lnr", "_ddm"))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(split(x, x$Illusion_Type), function(y) {
    data.frame(LNR = lq, "DDM-5" = pairs_q[[lq]], Illusion_Type = y$Illusion_Type[1], N = nrow(y),
               rho = stats::cor(y$Median_lnr, y$Median_ddm, method = "spearman"), check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}))
agree$Illusion_Type <- ill_all[agree$Illusion_Type]
agree_wide <- stats::reshape(agree[c("LNR", "DDM-5", "Illusion_Type", "rho")], idvar = c("LNR", "DDM-5"),
                             timevar = "Illusion_Type", direction = "wide")
names(agree_wide) <- sub("^rho\\.", "", names(agree_wide))
knitr::kable(agree_wide[c("LNR", "DDM-5", illusions, "All illusions")], digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

The illusion effect on P(error) (strength 0 to 1, mid difficulty) averaged
over each group's participants (the mean of their posterior medians, in
percentage points), against the typical participant of the section above:

```{r}
src <- list(LNR = lnr_ppt, "DDM-5" = ppt)
pe_ppt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(src), function(mn) {
  y <- src[[mn]][src[[mn]]$Quantity == "Illusion effect on P(error)" & src[[mn]]$Illusion_Type != "All", ]
  cbind(Model = mn, aggregate(list(Mean = 100 * y$Median), list(Illusion_Type = y$Illusion_Type, Group = y$Group), mean))
}))
pe_ppt$Illusion <- illusions[pe_ppt$Illusion_Type]
pe_ppt_wide <- stats::reshape(pe_ppt[c("Illusion", "Model", "Group", "Mean")], idvar = c("Illusion", "Model"),
                              timevar = "Group", direction = "wide")
names(pe_ppt_wide) <- sub("^Mean\\.", "", names(pe_ppt_wide))
knitr::kable(pe_ppt_wide[order(pe_ppt_wide$Illusion, match(pe_ppt_wide$Model, names(fits))),
                         c("Illusion", "Model", names(group_col))], digits = 0, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6.5

shown <- c("Non-decision time (s), no illusion", "Discriminability, no illusion",
           "Illusion magnitude (strength / difficulty)")
sc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(shown, function(q) {
  a <- lnr_ppt[lnr_ppt$Quantity == q & lnr_ppt$Illusion_Type != "All", c("Participant", "Group", "Illusion_Type", "Median")]
  b <- ppt[ppt$Quantity == q & ppt$Illusion_Type != "All", c("Participant", "Illusion_Type", "Median")]
  cbind(Quantity = q, merge(a, b, by = c("Participant", "Illusion_Type"), suffixes = c("_lnr", "_ddm")))
}))
sc$Quantity <- factor(sub(", no illusion", "", sc$Quantity), levels = sub(", no illusion", "", shown))
sc$Illusion_Type <- factor(illusions[sc$Illusion_Type], levels = illusions)
sc$Group <- factor(sc$Group, levels = names(group_col))
ggplot(sc, aes(Median_lnr, Median_ddm, colour = Group)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ Quantity + Illusion_Type, scales = "free", ncol = 3,
             labeller = function(l) label_value(l, multi_line = FALSE)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_col) +
  labs(x = "LNR (participant posterior median)", y = "DDM-5", colour = NULL,
       title = "The same participants in the two models",
       caption = "Strength 0, mid difficulty. Each panel has its own scales.") +
  theme_igsa + theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 7))
```

### Across illusions

The paper reports that the illusion magnitude correlates only weakly between
illusions, against a strongly shared general performance. The Spearman
correlation of the participant medians between each pair of illusions, per
model (`4_lnr_correlates.qmd` gives the LNR's per draw, with intervals; this
is the cruder correlation of medians, computed the same way for both):

```{r}
cross <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("Illusion magnitude (strength / difficulty)", "Illusion effect on discriminability",
                                 "Precision (difficulty slope)", "Discriminability, no illusion"), function(q) {
  src <- list(LNR = lnr_ppt, "DDM-5" = ppt)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(src), function(mn) {
    x <- src[[mn]]
    w <- x[x$Quantity == q & x$Illusion_Type != "All", c("Participant", "Illusion_Type", "Median")]
    w <- stats::reshape(w, idvar = "Participant", timevar = "Illusion_Type", direction = "wide")
    p <- utils::combn(names(illusions), 2)
    data.frame(Quantity = q, Pair = apply(p, 2, function(k) paste(illusions[k], collapse = " & ")), Model = mn,
               rho = apply(p, 2, function(k) stats::cor(w[[paste0("Median.", k[1])]], w[[paste0("Median.", k[2])]],
                                                         method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")))
  }))
}))
cross_wide <- stats::reshape(cross, idvar = c("Quantity", "Pair"), timevar = "Model", direction = "wide")
names(cross_wide) <- sub("^rho\\.", "", names(cross_wide))
knitr::kable(cross_wide, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

### What age accounts for

The paper's covariate check, done crudely here for both models: each
participant's median averaged over the illusions, regressed on Group, then
on Group and age (per decade). `4_lnr_correlates.qmd` does it per posterior
draw for the LNR. Coefficients with 95% confidence intervals.

```{r}
age_q <- list(
  "Non-decision time (ms)" = c(LNR = "Non-decision time (s), no illusion", "DDM-5" = "Non-decision time (s), no illusion"),
  "Caution (LNR: speed; DDM-5: boundary)" = c(LNR = "Speed, no illusion", "DDM-5" = "Boundary, no illusion"),
  "Discriminability" = c(LNR = "Discriminability, no illusion", "DDM-5" = "Discriminability, no illusion"),
  "Illusion magnitude" = c(LNR = "Illusion magnitude (strength / difficulty)", "DDM-5" = "Illusion magnitude (strength / difficulty)")
)
ages <- unique(lnr_ppt[c("Participant", "Age")])
age_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(age_q), function(lab) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits), function(mn) {
    src <- if (mn == "LNR") lnr_ppt else ppt
    y <- src[src$Quantity == age_q[[lab]][[mn]] & src$Illusion_Type == "All", c("Participant", "Group", "Median")]
    y <- merge(y, ages, by = "Participant")
    y$Group <- factor(y$Group, levels = names(group_col))
    y$Decade <- y$Age / 10
    k <- if (grepl("ms", lab)) 1000 else 1
    fit1 <- stats::lm(k * Median ~ Group, data = y[!is.na(y$Age), ])
    fit2 <- stats::lm(k * Median ~ Group + Decade, data = y)
    f <- function(fit, term) {
      ci <- stats::confint(fit)[term, ]
      fmt_ci(stats::coef(fit)[[term]], ci[1], ci[2], digits = if (k == 1000) 0 else 2)
    }
    data.frame(Quantity = lab, Model = mn, N = stats::nobs(fit2),
               "Past - Never" = f(fit1, "GroupPast"), "Recent - Never" = f(fit1, "GroupRecent"),
               "Past - Never, age-adjusted" = f(fit2, "GroupPast"), "Recent - Never, age-adjusted" = f(fit2, "GroupRecent"),
               "Age, per decade" = f(fit2, "Decade"), check.names = FALSE)
  }))
}))
knitr::kable(age_tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Summary: should the paper switch?

```{r}
# The numbers quoted below, from the sections above.
pick <- function(model, q, contrast, ill = "All") {
  x <- avg[avg$Model == model & avg$Quantity == q & avg$Contrast == contrast & avg$Illusion_Type == ill, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(x) == 1)
  x
}
say <- function(x, digits = 2) fmt_ci(x$Median, x$CI_low, x$CI_high, digits)
dev <- function(model, measure, col) dev_tab[dev_tab$Model == model & dev_tab$Measure == measure, col]
qdev <- function(model, response, p) round(q_tab$Absolute[q_tab$Model == model & q_tab$Response == response & q_tab$Quantile == p])
vs_never <- ic[ic$Contrast != "Recent - Past", ]
n_credible <- function(model) sum(vs_never$pd[vs_never$Model == model] >= 0.975)
rel_range <- function(model, contrast) {
  r <- -ic$Median_rel[ic$Model == model & ic$Contrast == contrast]
  sprintf("%.0f–%.0f%%", min(r), max(r))
}
rho <- function(lq) agree$rho[agree$LNR == lq & agree$Illusion_Type == "All illusions"]
# The range, over illusions and both user groups, of a component's change
# relative to Never (medians, %).
rel_comp <- function(model, q) {
  r <- index_relative$Median[index_relative$Model == model & index_relative$Quantity == q &
                               index_relative$Contrast != "Recent - Past"]
  sprintf("%+.0f to %+.0f%%", min(r), max(r))
}
age_cell <- function(q, model, col) age_tab[age_tab$Quantity == q & age_tab$Model == model, col]
ndt_q <- "Non-decision time (ms)"
```

**Fit: the DDM-5 predicts the data better.** Its cross-validated log
predictive density is ahead by `r sprintf("%.0f", elpd_gap)` (SE
`r sprintf("%.0f", elpd_gap_se)`) with fewer effective parameters (p_loo
`r sprintf("%.0f", loo_tab$p_loo[loo_tab$Model == "DDM-5"])` against
`r sprintf("%.0f", loo_tab$p_loo[loo_tab$Model == "LNR"])`), with the Pareto k
caveat above. Its median response times are off by
`r sprintf("%.0f", dev("DDM-5", "Median RT (ms)", "Mean absolute"))` ms on
average against `r sprintf("%.0f", dev("LNR", "Median RT (ms)", "Mean absolute"))`
for the LNR, with `r dev("DDM-5", "Median RT (ms)", "Inside the 95% band")`
of the observed medians inside its 95% band against
`r dev("LNR", "Median RT (ms)", "Inside the 95% band")`. The error rates are
close in both (off by `r sprintf("%.1f", dev("DDM-5", "Error rate (points)", "Mean absolute"))`
and `r sprintf("%.1f", dev("LNR", "Error rate (points)", "Mean absolute"))`
points). The shape of the distributions is better in places, not everywhere.
With no illusion, its distributions are more peaked than the LNR's, closer to
the observed ones (the LNR's main misfit), though still short of the
observed peak in places. The slow half of the correct response times is
closer (70th and 90th
percentiles off by `r qdev("DDM-5", "Correct", 0.7)` and
`r qdev("DDM-5", "Correct", 0.9)` ms, against `r qdev("LNR", "Correct", 0.7)`
and `r qdev("LNR", "Correct", 0.9)`). The slow tail of the errors is not
(90th percentile off by `r qdev("DDM-5", "Error", 0.9)` ms, against
`r qdev("LNR", "Error", 0.9)`).

**Sampling: much better.** It has `r diag_tab["DDM-5", "Divergent"]`
divergent transitions (LNR: `r diag_tab["LNR", "Divergent"]`), a max Rhat of
`r diag_tab["DDM-5", "max Rhat"]` against `r diag_tab["LNR", "max Rhat"]` on
the population coefficients and of `r diag_tab["DDM-5", "max Rhat "]` against
`r diag_tab["LNR", "max Rhat "]` on the participant ones, a minimum bulk ESS
per draw of `r diag_tab["DDM-5", "min bulk ESS / draw"]` against
`r diag_tab["LNR", "min bulk ESS / draw"]`, and shards of 4–5 h against
7–32 h. None of the LNR's caveats on convergence would be needed.

**The group story: mostly the same, with the slowness in a parameter with a
standard name.** Averaged over the design and the illusions (median and 95%
interval):

- **Caution.** Users have a wider boundary: Past − Never
  `r say(pick("DDM-5", "boundary", "Past - Never"))`, Recent − Never
  `r say(pick("DDM-5", "boundary", "Recent - Never"))`. This is the LNR's
  slower accumulators under another name: participants' LNR speed and DDM-5
  boundary correlate at ρ = `r sprintf("%.2f", rho("Speed, no illusion"))`.
- **Non-decision time.** The LNR's
  `r say(pick("LNR", "ndt", "Past - Never"), 0)` and
  `r say(pick("LNR", "ndt", "Recent - Never"), 0)` ms become
  `r say(pick("DDM-5", "ndt", "Past - Never"), 0)` and
  `r say(pick("DDM-5", "ndt", "Recent - Never"), 0)` ms. In the crude
  participant-level check, age accounts for all of it
  (age-adjusted: `r age_cell(ndt_q, "DDM-5", "Past - Never, age-adjusted")`
  and `r age_cell(ndt_q, "DDM-5", "Recent - Never, age-adjusted")` ms). The
  paper's longer non-decision time in users, and its age caveat, would
  mostly go.
- **Errors.** Both models give users fewer errors: Recent − Never
  `r say(pick("LNR", "perror", "Recent - Never"), 1)` points (LNR) and
  `r say(pick("DDM-5", "perror", "Recent - Never"), 1)` (DDM-5).
- **Discriminability.** In the DDM-5, Recent users are ahead of Past users
  (Recent − Past `r say(pick("DDM-5", "delta", "Recent - Past"))`, pd
  `r sprintf("%.3f", pick("DDM-5", "delta", "Recent - Past")$pd)`), which the
  LNR does not show (`r say(pick("LNR", "delta", "Recent - Past"))`). That
  is the one place where "Past and Recent barely differ" would no longer
  hold.
- **Illusion magnitude.** The same direction, larger and clearer:
  `r n_credible("DDM-5")` of the six user − Never contrasts have pd ≥ 0.975
  in the DDM-5, against `r n_credible("LNR")` in the LNR. Relative to Never,
  the magnitude is `r rel_range("DDM-5", "Past - Never")` smaller in Past
  users and `r rel_range("DDM-5", "Recent - Never")` in Recent users (LNR:
  `r rel_range("LNR", "Past - Never")` and `r rel_range("LNR", "Recent - Never")`),
  most on the Ebbinghaus. Recent − Past is nothing in either model.
  Participants' magnitudes agree between the models (ρ =
  `r sprintf("%.2f", rho("Illusion magnitude (strength / difficulty)"))`),
  and age does not move the group differences in either.
- **Where the smaller magnitude comes from.** In both models, users'
  precision term is steeper. They differ on the other component. In the
  LNR, users' illusion effect on discriminability is also larger than
  Never's, by `r rel_comp("LNR", "delta_strength")`. That is the paper's
  steeper slope in users, which its Discussion has to reconcile with the
  smaller magnitude. In the DDM-5 it is about the same as Never's
  (`r rel_comp("DDM-5", "delta_strength")`). So the illusion costs users as
  much drift as anyone, and only the real difference has a larger effect on
  theirs. That story is simpler, and it needs no reconciling.

**What speaks against it, as fitted.** Its boundary and start point vary
with illusion strength. Never's boundary is `r sprintf("%.2f", a_fac["Never"])`
on the most facilitating trials and `r sprintf("%.2f", a_con["Never"])` on
the most conflicting ones. Its start point is `r sprintf("%.2f", w_fac["Never"])`
and `r sprintf("%.2f", w_con["Never"])`. The strengths are mixed at random
within blocks, and a diffusion model reads both parameters as set before the
stimulus. So this is the first thing a reviewer would object to, and it
weakens the interpretability that is the reason to switch. The LNR has no
parameter of that kind (its threshold is fixed). Discriminability is also
the quantity whose meaning changes most with the switch: participants'
estimates agree only moderately between the models (ρ =
`r sprintf("%.2f", rho("Discriminability, no illusion"))`).

**Next step.** Refit the DDM-5 with the boundary and the start point
depending on Group and illusion only, not on strength or difficulty, and
repeat this comparison on it. The illusions are blocked, so a boundary per
illusion is legitimate. If the caution and illusion-magnitude results hold
there, the DDM is the clearer model for the paper.
